newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-BEVAN, SLATER REVIVE AUSTRALIAN HOPES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BEVAN, SLATER REVIVE AUSTRALIAN HOPES.

text.p: Fighting half-centuries by Michael Bevan and Michael Slater helped Australia reach 238 for six against South Africa in the Titan Cup triangular limited-over series on Friday.
Left-handed Bevan made a career-best 79 and added 124 runs from 122 deliveries for the fifth wicket with Slater to help Australia overcome a slow scoring rate and a middle-order slump.
Bevan faced 70 balls and struck seven boundaries to reach his eighth half-century in one-day internationals. Slater remained unbeaten on 53 from 68 balls which included four boundaries.
Bevan's previous best in one-dayers was 78 against the West Indies in Sydney last season.
The pair came to the wicket after left-arm spinner Nicy Boje dismissed Steve Waugh and Ricky Ponting with successive balls to leave Australia tottering at 113 for four in the 29th over.
Skipper Mark Taylor, Stuart Law and Waugh all made good starts but fell trying to accelerate the run-rate.
Law, promoted to open the innings, struck 22 from 17 balls including four boundaries.
Taylor and Waugh (37) steadied the innings with a 56-run second-wicket stand off 99 balls.
Taylor scored 38 runs from 76 balls with two fours before becoming off-spinner Pat Symcox's lone victim, caught by Jonty Rhodes at mid-wicket.
